text:
maria: seeing a big out-of-band latency spike in us-west-2 since 06:02 UTC. PXE boots are timing out and provisioning retries are saturating the GPU pool. SLA for Dedicated customers is degrading. Anyone else seeing this?

jake: looking now. which fleet? rack tags?

maria: affected: gpu-pool-uw2-prod (racks: r11-r14). interrupts: high BMC RTT, IPMI sessions piling up. example from one host: 
```
Jun 14 06:05:12 host-r11-03 bmc: ipmi_read: timeout after 12000ms
Jun 14 06:05:12 host-r11-03 bmc: cmd_queue: 42 pending, conn_count=87
Jun 14 06:05:13 host-r11-03 pxe: tftp fetch failed: ECONNRESET
Jun 14 06:05:14 provisioning: retrying (attempt 3) for host-r11-03
```

ops-bot: ALERT: oob.bmc.latency spike detected (avg RTT 2.8s -> 12.4s) on cluster gpu-pool-uw2-prod. Triggered at 1718504309.

nina: that timeframe aligns with the microcode roll we did last night to mitigate CVE-2024-xxxx. Did we flip any secure-boot flags during that batch?

maria: we rolled microcode + BMC fw (v2.3.8 -> v2.3.10) overnight, but secureboot flag should be unchanged. deployment job log: `deploy-bmc-fw us-west-2: job/5991 succeeded with 98%`

jake: could be the fw introduced a regression in IPMI connection pooling. Quick check: do IPMI sessions leak? can we dump conn_count on a bad box?

maria: on host-r11-03: `ipmitool lan print` shows multiple stale sessions. conn table attached (excerpt): `sessions: 87 active, 0 closed`

ryan: customer support already pinged about elevated provisioning times for a Reserved customer. they're seeing queue depth climb and costing us on preemptible fallback. Estimated cost delta ~+$3.2k/day if this continues.

nina: short-term mitigation: reduce concurrent provisioning jobs per rack (backpressure), route new jobs to us-east-1/dedicated overflow, and mark a subset of r11 as maintenance to stop new allocations. Also suggest bumping BMC watchdog to force periodic resets.

jake: agree. I'm going to add a per-rack throttling rule: `provisioning.concurrent_per_rack=4` (was 12). Will also add a temporary route rule to prefer us-east-1 for new builds.

maria: started throttling on r11-r14. Observed immediate drop in IPMI queue on two hosts. clearing out pending retries now.

ops-bot: NOTE: routing rule `prefer-east` applied to gpu-pool-uw2-prod at 06:12 UTC.

nina: parallel track: we should validate the microcode/BMC batch. Rollback plan? Can we rollback BMC fw for the worst 20 hosts and observe?

maria: yes, I can queue rollback for r11-03 to r11-06. doing canary rollback now.

jake: if rollback helps, we do a staged rollback across r11-r14. But we should also capture pcap on BMC mgmt network to look for retrans/keepalive failures.

maria: rollback canary complete on r11-03..06, results: BMC RTT dropped to ~200ms, PXE success rate back to normal, provisioning queue drain started.

ryan: excellent — please keep customers updated. I'll open a brief incident note to sales/CS with the rollback state and cost impact estimate.

nina: follow-up items: 1) Reproduce failure in lab with fw v2.3.10 + secure-boot unchanged 2) Capture BMC mgmt pcap and ipmi logs for bug report to vendor 3) Add automated OOB health check that fails faster and autoslices provisioning load 4) Consider delaying microcode/bmc batch next time until e2e smoke passes provisioning path

maria: agreed. creating a postmortem ticket and tagging the fw release owner. For now leaving r11-07..14 in maintenance until we validate.

jake: added packet capture job scheduled for 06:45 UTC and a temporary k8s job to run ipmi session sweeper every 30s.

ops-bot: INCIDENT: oob-bmc-provisioning-uw2 created. Sev: P2. Incident channel: #incidents.incident-1721.

maria: timeline summary posted to the incident doc. immediate status: canary rollback successful, throttles in place, routing overflow enabled. Next update in 30m. :thumbsup:
